WRO 2026 RoboMission Senior · Robot 13

Mosaic Masters,
built in blocks

The Python program tracks where the robot is on the mat and works out every turn as it goes. Word blocks cannot do that — not in any sane number of blocks. So this is the same mission built the way blocks are good at: a measured sequence of face this heading, drive this far, with the gyro keeping every heading honest.

It is genuinely competitive; plenty of teams score well with exactly this. It is just less forgiving. Get one distance wrong and everything after it is wrong too, where the Python version re-derives its position at every step.

02

Headings

Every turn in this program is an absolute compass heading, never “turn left a bit”. That is the whole trick — errors stop piling up.

0° away from you, across the short side 270° ←——+——→ 90° to your right, along the long side 180° back towards you

Set the robot down in the ROBOMISSION corner facing along the mat, to the right. The gyro resets to zero wherever you place it, so every heading in the tables below is measured from that starting direction.

03

Setup

Under when program starts, in this order:

  1. Movement set movement motors to A E
  2. Movement set movement speed to 40 %
  3. Motors B set speed to 60 %
  4. Motors C set speed to 60 %
  5. Sensors reset yaw angle start direction becomes 0
  6. Motors C go to position 0 lift down
  7. Motors B go to position 0 grabber open
04

Build these three My Blocks first

Everything else is made of them. My Blocks → Make a Block.

FACE (heading) — turn to a gyro heading

The block that makes the whole thing work. Give it a number input called heading.

  1. Control repeat until abs( heading − yaw angle ) < 2
  2. Control if heading − yaw angle > 0 then
  3. Movement start moving with steering 100 right
  4. Control else
  5. Movement start moving with steering −100 left
  6. Movement stop moving
  7. Control wait 0.2 seconds

Drop the movement speed to about 20 % inside this block and put it back to 40 % after. A slow turn stops far more accurately.

GRAB — take one block

  1. Motors C go to position 0 lift down
  2. Motors B go to position 0 open
  3. Movement move 9 cm forward
  4. Motors B go to position 95 close on it
  5. Motors C go to position 160 lift clear
  6. Movement move 9 cm backward

PLACE — put it down

  1. Motors C go to position 10 lower onto the cell
  2. Motors B go to position 0 everything comes out
  3. Motors C go to position 160 raise first!
  4. Movement move 5 cm backward
The order in PLACE matters. Raising before you reverse is not fussiness — with the lift down, backing off scrapes the chassis over the block you just placed. This was a real bug in the Python version until the simulator caught it.
05

One trip

The same six steps every time. Repeat once per block.

FACE (heading to the depot) move (distance) cm FACE (the depot's facing) GRAB FACE (heading to the lane corner) move (distance) cm FACE 90 move (along the lane) cm FACE 0 move (run in) cm PLACE

Steps 3–4 · depot round to the lane corner

The lane corner is the one spot near the plate where it is safe to turn. Do not cut it. The robot is 25 cm wide and its corners sweep 15.4 cm when it spins, so turning any closer drags a corner over the tiles.

Fill the far row (row 0) first. The robot reaches over the near cells to get to the far ones, so doing row 0 first means it never reaches across a block it has already placed.

These distances come from the field map in the Python program. Two of its numbers are still guesses — the cell pitch and how far along the mat the plate sits — so measure those and the whole table shifts with them.

06

Reading the pattern

Blocks can read the mosaic with is F colour ___ ?. But the colour sensor is bolted to the chassis, so when the lift raises the robot to clear the plate the sensor rises with it and the readings get worse.

For a block program the practical answer is to look at the plate yourself before the run and use the matching sequence. The colour column in the table above is where you write down what you see.

07

Test it in this order

Do not build the whole thing and run it.

  1. Setup + FACE. Run FACE 90, FACE 180, FACE 0. Spinning the wrong way means swapping the two steering values inside FACE. Hunting back and forth means slowing it down or widening < 2 to < 3.
  2. move 50 cm. Measure what you actually get. If it comes out at 48, every distance in the tables needs multiplying by 50 ÷ 48.
  3. GRAB on a block sitting on the table.
  4. PLACE.
  5. One full trip to one cell.
  6. The rest of the trips.
